strengths: Recognizes an epithelial/pancreatic lineage and maps to a valid ontology term
weaknesses: Pancreatic ductal specificity rests on CA12, not a canonical ductal marker; canonical KRT19/CFTR/SOX9 absent; competing acinar and hepatocyte markers present

strengths: Conservative supported ancestor consistent with CA12/AQP8/DPEP1 epithelial-associated markers
Does not over-commit to an unsupported subtype amid conflicting signals
weaknesses: Broad label only; PRSS3/AQP8 acinar and ANGPTL3/SLC22A9 hepatocyte signals remain unresolved

strengths: Correctly flags liver/transport markers (SLC22A9, ANGPTL3, AQP8) and metabolic enrichment
weaknesses: Ambiguous mapping; hepatocyte branch lacks canonical hepatocyte markers (ALB/TTR/APOA2) and does not meaningfully outrank acinar/ductal alternatives

supporting: CA12, AQP8 and DPEP1 are top positive DEGs and are consistent with an epithelial identity (broad supported ancestor).
PRSS3 and AQP8 provide a weak pancreatic acinar signal, but no canonical PRSS1/CPA1/CEL acinar markers are present
ANGPTL3 and SLC22A9 provide a hepatocyte-like signal but no canonical ALB/TTR markers are present, so subtype refinement is not supported.
conflicting: ANGPTL3 and SLC22A9 favor a hepatocyte-like program
PRSS3 and AQP8 favor pancreatic acinar
CA12 alone is insufficient to establish pancreatic ductal identity
classic ductal (KRT19/CFTR/SOX9), acinar (PRSS1/CPA1/CEL), and hepatocyte (ALB/TTR/APOA2) markers are absent.
enrichment_or_literature: NR1H2 & NR1H3 regulate gene expression linked to lipogenesis
Uptake of dietary cobalamins into enterocytes
